note: The V1 baseline corpus. Requests are written the way real ones arrive -- lowercase, partial, sometimes self-contradictory -- because V1's intake is what is being measured and a tidied request measures a learner who does not exist. `corrections` exist because the correction path was exercised twice in 37 projects: without them the baseline measures a system nobody ever corrects.

cases.title: Agentic AI — interview preparation
cases.request: i need agentic ai notes for interview, from scratch
cases.why_this_case: The known failure. V1 produced an underfunded capability ('design iterative retrieval loops with query reformulation' over a scope holding one retrieval concept) and a cross-cutting 'advanced' bucket. Also the case where 'from scratch' was read as assuming ML literacy -- the provenance bug the register calls solved, re-tested here.

situation.purpose: Answer interview questions about agentic AI
situation.entry_point: Writes code; has not built an agent; 'from scratch' binds this
situation.target_capability: Explain, compare and justify choices under questioning
constraints: 'from scratch' is a stated constraint on entry point

intake_answers: i can code but i've never built an agent or used any of these frameworks
corrections: you've missed evaluation entirely - interviewers always ask how you'd know if the agent is working

must_not_become: a single 'Frameworks' node listing LangGraph, AutoGen and CrewAI together — the learner must tell them apart to answer 'why did you pick one'
an 'advanced topics' module holding safety, observability, cost, deployment and standards because they are all late
a capability promising design or architecture work when the job is orient
good_curriculum.capability_test: every clause must be answerable in an interview, and backed by a concept the module actually covers

watch_for: entry_point asserting prior literacy against 'from scratch'
parenthetical framework lists
unbacked capability clauses
cross-cutting leftovers module

cases.title: Transformers — deep understanding
cases.request: i want to properly understand transformers, not just the high level stuff. i've done linear algebra and i can read pytorch
cases.why_this_case: A rich, well-specified request: intake should ask almost nothing. Tests whether stated competence is honoured rather than re-asked, and whether 'properly understand' produces depth rather than breadth.

situation.purpose: Genuine understanding, not exam or interview
situation.target_capability: Explain why each component exists and what breaks without it

corrections: go deeper on attention - that's the part i actually want to understand

must_not_become: a survey that spends a module on 'history of NLP' before reaching attention
depth allocated evenly when the learner named attention as the target
good_curriculum.capability_test: capability should be in explain/justify register, and should not promise implementing a trained model unless training is actually covered

watch_for: questions asked about things the request already stated
breadth substituting for depth
maths depth inconsistent with stated linear algebra

cases.title: French Revolution — school exam revision
cases.request: french revolution notes for my class 9 history exam next week
cases.why_this_case: Non-technical, exam-shaped, with a real time constraint stated. Tests whether purpose=exam actually changes the curriculum (retrieve/rehearse, not construct) and whether a stated deadline reaches scope as depth pressure.

situation.purpose: Pass a school exam in a week
situation.entry_point: Class 9; has been taught the chapter once
situation.target_capability: Answer exam questions: causes, sequence, key figures, consequences

corrections: i don't need the economic theory stuff, the exam is mostly dates causes and people

must_not_become: a university-level treatment of revolutionary political philosophy
modules split by decade when the exam wants causes/events/consequences
good_curriculum.capability_test: capability must be in recall/answer register, not 'analyse the historiography'

watch_for: depth ignoring the one-week capacity
job read as 'construct' rather than retrieve/rehearse
non-technical subject producing a technical-shaped plan

cases.title: VLSI — deliberately underspecified
cases.why_this_case: The bare request. Six words, no purpose, no entry point, no target. This is the case the interpret/decide/ask split was built for (102s to 18s), and the one where V1 must ask rather than guess. Measures how many questions the budget actually spends and whether the options are materially different plans.

constraints: nothing is stated; every axis is the system's decision

intake_answers: it's for my university semester exam, i've done basic digital electronics

must_cover: depends entirely on the answer given at intake
must_not_become: a full plan derived with no question asked at all
questions whose options imply the same plan ('detailed' vs 'comprehensive')
good_curriculum.capability_test: after the intake answer, the plan must visibly reflect exam-purpose and the stated digital-electronics entry point

watch_for: verdict sufficient on a six-word request
questions written for axes the decider did not choose
options that are one option wearing two labels
any axis read as 'inferred' with a span covering the whole request

cases.title: Graph DSA — interview cheat sheet
cases.request: cheat sheet for graph dsa questions for my interview next month
cases.why_this_case: Artifact type is stated outright ('cheat sheet'), so it must be inferred and never asked. A cheat sheet is a look-up artifact, which is a different document job from orienting notes -- tests whether the job taxonomy actually changes treatment.

situation.entry_point: Knows basic data structures; has solved some problems
situation.target_capability: Recognise the pattern under time pressure and recall the approach

corrections: union-find isn't relevant for me, the companies i'm targeting don't ask it

must_not_become: a multi-module course — one subject, one sitting, one thing to walk in able to do
long prose explanations, when the artifact type stated is a cheat sheet
good_curriculum.capability_test: capability in look-up/recognise register, not 'implement from scratch'

watch_for: artifact_type asked despite being stated
partition splitting a cheat sheet into modules
depth 'work through' producing essays in a look-up artifact

cases.title: Indian Contract Act — source/authority-heavy
cases.request: i need to study the indian contract act 1872 for my law semester, section wise
cases.why_this_case: The case the register says broke assumptions that looked reasonable under a coding workload. The subject has a primary source that is READ, not derived: the Act is numbered sections, and a 'derived concept landscape' is the wrong operation. Tests whether V1 invents a structure where an authoritative one exists.

situation.entry_point: Law student, first exposure to contract law
situation.target_capability: State and apply the sections; answer problem questions
constraints: the Act is the authority, not the model's derivation

corrections: the ordering should follow the act's own sections, not your grouping

must_not_become: a derived conceptual landscape that renames or reorders statutory sections
a plan that silently invents a taxonomy the Act does not use
good_curriculum.capability_test: capability must involve stating and applying provisions; terminology must be the Act's

watch_for: derive_structure inventing concept names not in the Act
traversal that contradicts 'section wise'
no mechanism to say 'this needs the source text'
correction about ordering routed to partition rather than traversal

cases.title: Git commit messages — deliberately narrow
cases.request: how to write good git commit messages
cases.why_this_case: The partition floor. This is one small subject with one sitting's worth of material. plan_v3 says explicitly that length is never a reason to split and that most narrow requests are one module -- this measures whether that instruction holds. Over-partitioning here is the clearest possible signal that module count is not actually derived from scope.

situation.entry_point: Uses git daily; commits are messy
situation.target_capability: Write a commit message a reviewer can use

corrections: make it dark themed with orange accents

must_not_become: 'Part 1: Fundamentals' and 'Part 2: Advanced' — packaging, not a curriculum
a module per commit-message section

watch_for: module_count > 1 at all
the theme correction being absorbed into a plan decision instead of deferred as out_of_scope

cases.title: Heart anatomy — spatial content
cases.request: human heart structure and blood flow for neet, i need to be able to label diagrams
cases.why_this_case: Probes the representation boundary directly. 'Label diagrams' is a stated requirement for exactly the thing the system cannot produce: family E, perceptual-referent. The honest outcome is a reported limitation before approval, not prose standing in for a figure. Tests feasibility reporting end to end.

situation.target_capability: Label a heart diagram and trace blood flow
constraints: stated: label diagrams — spatial content is the target, not a nice-to-have

must_not_become: a plan claiming to teach diagram labelling with no acknowledgement that it cannot draw the diagram
a relation block of named parts standing in for a spatial figure
good_curriculum.capability_test: the plan must report, before approval, that the figures this target needs are not producible

watch_for: anticipates=perceptual-referent on the spatial concepts
feasibility.serves_everything true despite spatial targets
generation drawing boxes instead of emitting the stated-gap callout
stated_gaps count at generation

cases.title: Distributed consensus — stated treatment preference
cases.request: explain distributed consensus to me, raft and paxos. use lots of analogies and worked examples, i learn badly from formal definitions
cases.why_this_case: Aims straight at the gap found by code reading: `anticipates` never reaches the generator, and a stated treatment preference arrives at the unit prompt as one line among many with no machinery behind it. This case states the preference as plainly as a user can. If the artifact is not visibly analogy-heavy, the preference is decorative.

situation.purpose: Understand it well enough to reason about systems
situation.entry_point: Backend engineer; no distributed systems theory
situation.target_capability: Explain why consensus is hard and how Raft solves it
constraints: stated: learns badly from formal definitions

must_not_become: formal-definition-first treatment, which is what the learner said defeats them
a plan that records the preference and generates content that ignores it
good_curriculum.capability_test: treatment preference must survive into the generated artifact, measurably

watch_for: stated preference present in situation.stated but absent from the artifact
treatments_anticipated vs treatments_produced divergence
departures count and block mix in the generated module
analogy density in the produced text

cases.title: Machine learning in a weekend — conflicting request
cases.request: i want to master machine learning and be able to build production models, i have one weekend
cases.why_this_case: A request that cannot be satisfied as stated. Capacity and target are in direct conflict. The honest behaviours are: report the conflict, or scope to what a weekend genuinely buys and say plainly what was given up. The dishonest behaviour is a confident plan promising mastery. Tests whether consequence/extent reporting actually constrains the promise.

situation.target_capability: Stated as 'master ML and build production models' — not achievable in the stated capacity

intake_answers: i've written python for a few years but no ml at all
corrections: ok that's too much, what can i actually get done in two days

must_cover: depends on how the conflict is resolved — but the resolution must be visible
must_not_become: a plan whose capability still promises production ML after a weekend
an extent estimate that quietly exceeds the stated capacity with no comment
good_curriculum.capability_test: either the capability is honestly reduced, or the shortfall is stated in consequence/extent where the user can see it before approving

watch_for: capacity captured as a stated constraint at all
extent vs stated capacity
capability register after the correction
whether the correction about time routes to scope and interpret_situation
